item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-09-28
item.description: ## 今日发生了什么 今天论坛的主要动态是 Fiber 生态新应用与新讨论并行，Twine、FiberNuts 和 .cell 名称支付都有进展 [S01, S02, S07, S15]。节点收入层讨论继续发酵，逐步聚焦到节点旁报告器、公共统计站和 CKBadger 数据源 [S03, S04, S05]。同时，DAO Cycle Alerts 与 FNN Safeguard 等提案引发了隐私、安全、独特价值和资助合理性的追问 [S09, S13]。 ## 重点话题 Twine 的 Fiber P2P 买卖 CKB PoC 继续细化规则：quake 认为这个点子好、PoC 做得好，UI 已经让基本交易和争议解决流程清楚 [S01]；他建议下一步明确证据如何验证、谁能采取哪些行动、争议时谁负责 [S01]。ebubedev 回应说规则已经写下来，守护进程测试会在支付、超时或争议破坏规则时失败 [S02]；法币不进入协议，收据是买家上传的 JPEG/PNG，求解器会读取图片、聊天和订单 [S02]。 CKB 节点收入层讨论转向“信任先于金钱”：psawyerberlin 总结说节点运营者已有非货币回报（免信任、隐私），服务收入只有确实带来更多全节点才对 CKB 有帮助 [S03]。LusoCryptoLabs 指出第一步与 Jan 的 CKB Node Ninjas 提案相同，即节点旁守护进程和 ethstats 风格网站，由 Community DAO 资助 [S04]。psawyerberlin 确认这本质上与 CKB Node Ninjas 是同一想法，并认为...

item.title: Twine: Buy and Sell CKB Without Depositing on an Exchange (Fiber P2P PoC) (2 posts)
item.description: I think this is a good idea, and the PoC is well done. The UI already makes the basic trading and dispute resolution flows clear For the next step, I suggest adding more on defining clear rules: how evidence is verified, who can take which actions, and who is responsible when something goes wrong. Tests showing that these rules hold up when payments fail, time out, or are disputed would go a long way toward building trust. Thanks Quake. I took that approach: the rules are written down, and the daemon tests fail if a payment, a timeout, or a dispute breaks them. Fiat stays off the protocol. item.title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes (4 posts)
item.description: Where this thread has led me: trust before money Thanks to everyone who contributed. A few points changed my thinking: @janx: node operators already get non-monetary returns (trustlessness, privacy), and service income only helps CKB if it actually brings more full nodes. @joshyates1980: many of us run nodes simply to support Nervos, and some recognition would already mean a lot. @LusoCryptoLabs: light-client serving is a service only a real full node can provide, and it has to stay free. So my conclusion: any service layer must stay outside the node, as a separate, optional tool, never part of ckb itself. And trust has to come before money. item.title: FiberNuts Community Market: A Testnet App for Cashu + Fiber (1 posts)
item.description: Gm CKB community, In my earlier FiberNuts post, I said the next step should be more than improving the wallet. It should be a high-level application that shows why Cashu + Fiber could be useful in an everyday setting. That application is now built: FiberNuts Community Market. The idea is a small community event where attendees can buy items or tip contributors with RUSD ecash, while vendors receive and secure those payments before cashing out through Fiber. Fiber moves RUSD into and out of the system. Cashu handles the many lightweight payments in between. item.title: Research Notes: What Zero-Knowledge Proofs Enable on CKB (1 posts)
item.description: Thanks, Cecilia. Great feedback. I’m tentatively targeting initial ZK support for 0.32, and expect to incorporate much of your feedback: one exact verifier profile first, explicit VK and codec identities, a defined context-binding envelope, and measurements of the actual Spawn/IPC path. I’ll take the integration and remaining validation forward on the CellScript side.

item.title: CellScript 0.30: Abstractions, Bytes, and the Cost (1 posts)
item.description: A follow-up on the immediate encoding mentioned in section 5. I gave it one sentence and a byte count there, which skipped over what the compiler was actually doing. The work on 0.31 makes that worth revisiting. The original post recorded a 464-byte saving from shorter constant loads. That came from a fairly simple improvement developed on 0.26b and carried into 0.30: stop using two instructions when one will do. For anyone who doesn’t usually read assembly, an immediate is a number written directly into an instruction. “Add 5 to this register” carries the 5 in the instruction itself. A register is one of the small storage locations the machine uses while calculating. There is only so...

item.title: Paying a .cell name over Fiber on testnet: what it took (1 posts)
item.description: fiber-card3200×1800 251 KB In early September we checked whether a .cell name can work as a Fiber payment endpoint: a payer reads the name, finds the node, and pays it without asking the payee for anything. On testnet it did, including a payment routed through a public hub. Two things had to be fixed on the payee’s side first, and they are the useful part of this post. The records A name publishes two records: fiber.node: the node’s public key, 33 raw bytes. Fiber’s RPC takes it as bare hex in target_pubkey, so strip any 0x prefix at that boundary. fiber.addr: a multiaddr, as text. There is no invoice record.
